accepted_units.title: Compact objects form a bounded skeleton whose closure reconstructs an unbounded category
accepted_units.why_material: Injective resolutions of noetherian objects are shown compact and jointly detect every nonzero object, so the compact subcategory identifies with the bounded derived category. The ambient homotopy category is then characterized as the smallest triangulated category containing that skeleton and closed under coproducts, paralleling completion of finitely presented objects under filtered colimits.
accepted_units.context_note: The result assumes a locally noetherian Grothendieck category and uses injective resolutions; the completion analogy is explicit rather than an asserted equivalence of all completion notions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The injective-complex presentation supplies the ambient category, while compact generation and reconstruction by triangles and coproducts are invariant categorical properties.

accepted_units.title: Localization and adjoints produce orthogonal pieces and a functorial decomposition triangle
accepted_units.why_material: A localization sequence is characterized through fully faithful adjoints, a quotient equivalence, mutual orthogonality, and a canonical triangle splitting any object into kernel and localized components. Brown representability turns preservation of coproducts or products into practical criteria for constructing the required adjoints.
accepted_units.context_note: Several categorical diagrams have flattened arrows, but the enumerated axioms, equivalences, triangle, and adjoint criteria are legible in prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The diagram orientation depends on chosen inclusion and quotient functors; the universal roles of kernel, quotient, adjoints, and orthogonal pieces do not.

accepted_units.title: Localization yields a canonical replacement that computes the quotient category
accepted_units.why_material: The homotopy category of injectives localizes by acyclic complexes to the derived category. Its right adjoint selects K-injective representatives, giving every complex a functorial triangle with an acyclic error term and converting quotient morphisms into ordinary homotopy morphisms against the replacement.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is specialized to locally noetherian Grothendieck categories, but the replacement-via-adjoint mechanism is generic; the examples at the end state boundary cases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses injective complexes as representatives; the semantics are that a right adjoint chooses a canonical representative orthogonal to the discarded subcategory.

accepted_units.title: Compact generation upgrades one-sided localization to recollement
accepted_units.why_material: Compact objects constrain boundedness, and an equivalence on compact generators is extended through coproduct closure to construct the missing left adjoint. Combining localization and colocalization gives a recollement, so an ambient category can be reconstructed from complementary pieces with both projection directions available.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument relies on compact generation of the derived category; the corollary on products of acyclic injective complexes is a consequence, not the core accepted mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The categories are presented through injective complexes and derived quotients, whereas the passage from compact control to a two-sided gluing pattern is categorical.

accepted_units.title: Stabilization quotients away perfect information and retains the compact singular part
accepted_units.why_material: The stable derived category is obtained as the acyclic side of a recollement, and stabilization is the composite of the corresponding adjoints. On compact objects it agrees, up to direct factors, with the bounded category modulo compact or perfect objects, making precise which regular information is forgotten and which obstruction-like residue remains.
accepted_units.context_note: The equivalence on compact objects is explicitly only up to direct factors; that qualification must be retained in downstream use.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The chosen model uses acyclic injective complexes; the quotient semantics and compact singular residue are stable under equivalent categorical presentations.

accepted_units.title: A derived functor lifts to a larger category, with compatibility controlled by acyclic preservation
accepted_units.why_material: An additive functor is extended from derived categories to homotopy categories of injectives, and representability supplies adjoints under coproduct hypotheses. A natural comparison with the ordinary derived functor is an isomorphism exactly when acyclic injective complexes remain acyclic, isolating a concrete obstruction to commuting a construction with localization.
accepted_units.context_note: The small algebra example exhibits failure of the compatibility square; exact diagram arrows and the example complex should be checked against the PDF if reproduced.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The lift depends on injective and DG presentations, while the obstruction criterion—preservation of the kernel of localization—is presentation-independent.

accepted_units.title: Adjoints transfer a functor coherently across ambient, derived, compact, and stable levels
accepted_units.why_material: For an exact functor on noetherian objects, adjunction lifts it to injective homotopy categories and descends it to stable categories. Compatibility squares and compactness preservation show that its action on the stable compact quotient is determined by the bounded functor, providing a reusable method for moving one operation through several equivalent or localized representations.
accepted_units.context_note: Large commutative diagrams are extraction-damaged, but their direction is restated in the theorem and proof. Some final generalizations are explicitly tentative remarks.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction uses chosen adjoints and localizations; its core claim is coherence of the induced maps under passage among related categorical presentations.

accepted_units.title: Support decomposes an object, and removing a regular locus preserves singular information
accepted_units.why_material: Restriction to an open subspace splits injective objects by support and yields a triangle separating the part on the open set from the part on its complement. Quotienting by complement-supported objects gives the restricted category; if the open contains every singular point, the stable category and the bounded quotient by perfect complexes are unchanged.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion assumes separated noetherian schemes and finite Krull dimension for the singular-locus corollary; equivalence of the bounded quotient is stated only up to direct factors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Support and open restriction are geometric, but the generic move is localization by a kernel subcategory followed by an invariance test when the discarded region contributes no obstruction.

accepted_units.title: A left adjoint constructs complete resolutions and universal Gorenstein-injective approximations
accepted_units.why_material: Totally acyclic complexes are linked equivalently to Gorenstein-injective objects by taking a cycle. Orthogonality inside the compactly generated stable category gives a left adjoint to their inclusion; applying it to an injective resolution constructs a complete resolution and, after taking a cycle, a universal approximation characterized by a bijection of stable morphisms.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is within a locally noetherian Grothendieck category with compactly generated derived category; stable Hom decorations are visually degraded but the universal property is explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The complete complex is a representative; the approximation is canonical through its adjunction, not through a unique componentwise resolution.

accepted_units.title: A functorial complete resolution turns stable morphisms into a two-sided cohomological invariant
accepted_units.why_material: Tate cohomology is defined from the complete-resolution adjoint and equivalently as graded morphisms between stabilized objects. Functoriality supplies comparison maps and exact triangles yield long exact sequences, while several vanishing conditions collapse to equivalent obstruction tests.
accepted_units.context_note: Exact group formulas and decorations suffer some glyph loss; the accepted content is the equivalence of constructions, exactness mechanism, and vanishing semantics rather than coefficient-level calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One formula uses Hom into a complete injective resolution and another uses morphisms in a stable category; their natural isomorphism is precisely the useful representation bridge.

accepted_units.title: Orthogonality classes yield complementary universal approximations
accepted_units.why_material: Objects with vanishing Tate obstruction and Gorenstein-injective objects form complementary classes. Every object lies in two exact sequences exchanging the classes, the induced maps are right and left adjoints to their inclusions, and the intersection consists exactly of injectives. This packages approximation as both decomposition and a universal property.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is formulated in the stable category modulo injectives and uses complete resolutions; equality of the classes is not asserted outside the stated compact-generation assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact sequences depend on chosen representatives, while the adjoint approximation functors and orthogonality classes are canonical up to isomorphism.

accepted_units.title: Vanishing, total acyclicity, and stabilization equivalence characterize one structural regime
accepted_units.why_material: The injective Gorenstein property is characterized equivalently by an Ext-orthogonality condition, total acyclicity of all acyclic injective complexes, identification of two object classes, annihilation of injectives by stabilization, and equivalence between stable and Gorenstein-injective categories. This turns several differently presented tests into interchangeable diagnostics.
accepted_units.context_note: The later ring and scheme cases are examples under additional finiteness hypotheses and should not be read as proving the equivalences in arbitrary categories.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The criteria live in Ext groups, complexes, object classes, functor kernels, and category equivalences; their equivalence explicitly bridges those representations.

accepted_units.title: Tensoring with resolution objects realizes localization adjoints and stabilization
accepted_units.why_material: The injective and acyclic subcategories are tensor ideals. Tensoring with an injective resolution realizes the adjoint selecting injective complexes, while tensoring with a Tate resolution realizes stabilization and induces an equivalence with the stable module category. An abstract localization operation is thus represented by multiplication with distinguished objects.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem assumes modules over a finite-dimensional cocommutative Hopf algebra; the monoidal realization should not be generalized without checking tensor-ideal and adjunction hypotheses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The distinguished resolution objects depend on the module model, but their role as idempotent-like selectors for complementary tensor ideals is structural.

accepted_units.title: Compact generators reconstruct a homotopy category as a DG-derived category
accepted_units.why_material: A generating class is enriched by complexes of morphisms to form a small DG category. The Yoneda-style Hom representation preserves coproducts, is fully faithful by generation, and is essentially surjective because free DG modules generate, yielding an equivalent algebraic presentation of the original homotopy category.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses infinite devissage and assumes the chosen objects are compact generators; direct-sum and DG decorations are partially flattened in extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The DG category depends on a generating class and chosen resolutions, while its derived category recovers the same localizing category up to equivalence.

accepted_units.title: Every injective complex splits into a minimal part and a null-homotopic part
accepted_units.why_material: Homotopical minimality is characterized equivalently by absence of a nonzero contractible summand and by cycle inclusions being injective envelopes. Iteratively splitting explicit contractible pieces produces a decomposition into minimal and null-homotopic summands, and any two such decompositions have isomorphic minimal parts.
accepted_units.context_note: Some direct-sum symbols are lost in the normalized text, but the construction, three equivalent criteria, and uniqueness statement are clear from prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contractible complement is not claimed unique, whereas the minimal summand is canonical up to isomorphism; this distinction is central to the unit.
